records.source: וָאָשׁ֕וּב וָאֶשָּׂ֥א עֵינַ֖י וָֽאֶרְאֶ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה מְגִלָּ֥ה עָפָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I returned and lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a scroll flying.
pieces: Again I looked up, and I saw a flying scroll.

L.1: And again I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a flying scroll!

R.1: I looked up again and saw a scroll flying through the air.

decisions.choice: the sixth vision: a flying scroll, the curse that removes thieves and perjurers from the land
decisions.reason: Zechariah sees a huge scroll flying, and the angel explains it as the curse that goes out over the land against those who steal and those who swear falsely (verses 3-4). The vision follows the cleansing of the high priest (chapter 3): now wrongdoing is purged from the land itself. The next vision (verses 5-11) carries wickedness away altogether.

decisions.choice: a scroll: a long sheet of leather or papyrus, written on and rolled up
decisions.reason: Books were written on scrolls (Jeremiah 36:2). This one is unrolled, so that it can be seen flying. Ezekiel saw a scroll written on front and back with lament and woe (Ezekiel 2:9-10).

decisions.choice: I returned and lifted up my eyes: I looked up again
decisions.reason: The verb "returned" is used with another verb to mean doing something again. On "lifted up my eyes", see 2:1.

decisions.choice: Again I looked up (B); I looked up again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "looked up" for the idiom, as in 2:1, and Readable adds "through the air" to make the picture plain.

records.heading: The flying scroll and the woman in the basket

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲנִ֤י רֹאֶה֙ מְגִלָּ֣ה עָפָ֔ה אָרְכָּהּ֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וְרָחְבָּ֖הּ עֶ֥שֶׂר בָּאַמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, What [are] you seeing? And I said, I [am] seeing a scroll flying; its length twenty by the cubit, and its width ten by the cubit.
pieces: He asked me, "What do you see?" I answered, "A flying scroll, {{units:about thirty feet|twenty cubits}} long and {{units:about fifteen feet|ten cubits}} wide."

L.2: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a scroll flying; its length [is] twenty by the cubit, and its width ten by the cubit."

R.2: He asked me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a flying scroll. It is {{units:about thirty feet|twenty cubits}} long and {{units:about fifteen feet|ten cubits}} wide."

decisions.choice: twenty cubits by ten: about thirty feet by fifteen, an enormous scroll
decisions.reason: A cubit was about 18 inches (see Genesis 6:15). No real scroll was so wide: this one is meant to be seen from far off by everyone. Its measurements are those of the porch in front of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:3), and some take the likeness to mean that the curse goes out from the LORD's presence. The angel does not explain the size.

decisions.choice: about thirty feet (twenty cubits); about fifteen feet (ten cubits)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the size in modern measures with the units setting, and the cubits as its alternative. Literal keeps the cubits.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֹ֚את הָֽאָלָ֔ה הַיּוֹצֵ֖את עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֣י כָל־הַגֹּנֵ֗ב מִזֶּה֙ כָּמ֣וֹהָ נִקָּ֔ה וְכָל־הַנִּ֨שְׁבָּ֔ע מִזֶּ֖ה כָּמ֥וֹהָ נִקָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, This [is] the curse which [is] going out over [the] face of all the land; for every one stealing, from here according to it has been purged, and every one swearing, from here according to it has been purged.
pieces: Then he said to me, "This is the curse that is going out over the whole land. As one side of it says, every thief will be swept away; and as the other side says, everyone who swears falsely will be swept away.

L.3: And he said to me, "This [is] the curse that is going forth over the face of the whole land; for everyone who steals will be purged out from here according to it, and everyone who swears will be purged out from here according to it.

R.3: Then he said to me, "This is the curse that is going out over the whole land. One side of the scroll says that everyone who steals will be removed from the land. The other side says that everyone who swears falsely will be removed too.

decisions.choice: the curse: the curse written into God's covenant against those who break it
decisions.reason: The word is used for the oath that binds people to the covenant and the curses that fall on those who break it (Deuteronomy 29:11, 13, 19-20). The scroll is that written curse, now set loose against wrongdoers.

decisions.choice: will be purged out: will be cleared away from the land
decisions.reason: The verb means to be cleaned out, emptied, or acquitted. In the form used here it often means "go unpunished" (Exodus 21:19; Jeremiah 25:29), and some read the verse as a complaint: until now every thief has gone unpunished. The translation reads it as the result of the curse: the land will be cleansed of thieves and perjurers, which fits verse 4.

decisions.choice: from here ... according to it: as written on one side of the scroll and on the other
alternatives: from this place, according to the curse
decisions.reason: The words "from this" can mean "from here", that is, from the land, or "on this side", as in Exodus 32:15, where the tablets were written "on this side and on that side". Read the second way, one side of the scroll condemns stealing and the other swearing falsely. Both readings keep the point: the curse removes such people.

decisions.choice: stealing and swearing falsely: two of the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: "You shall not steal" and "You shall not misuse the name of the LORD" (Exodus 20:7, 15) stand for the whole law: one sin wrongs a neighbor, the other wrongs God. Verse 4 makes plain that the swearing meant is swearing falsely by the LORD's name (Leviticus 19:12).

decisions.choice: as one side ... as the other side says (B); One side of the scroll says (R); swears falsely (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading of the two sides (m3) and say "swears falsely", which verse 4 makes plain. "Swept away" (B) and "removed from the land" (R) give the sense chosen in m2.

records.source: הוֹצֵאתִ֗יהָ נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּבָ֨אָה֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַגַּנָּ֔ב וְאֶל־בֵּ֛ית הַנִּשְׁבָּ֥ע בִּשְׁמִ֖י לַשָּׁ֑קֶר וְלָ֨נֶה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ בֵּית֔וֹ וְכִלַּ֖תּוּ וְאֶת־עֵצָ֥יו וְאֶת־אֲבָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: I have sent it out, declaration of Yahweh of hosts, and it will enter into [the] house of the thief and into [the] house of the one swearing by my name to falsehood, and it will lodge in [the] midst of his house and finish it, and its timbers and its stones.
pieces: I have sent it out, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, and it will go into the thief's house and the house of anyone who swears falsely by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. It will stay inside that house and destroy it, timber and stones alike."

L.4: I have sent it out, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, and it will come into the house of the thief and into the house of the one who swears by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name falsely; and it will lodge in the midst of {{gender:their|his}} house and consume it, both its timber and its stones."

R.4: I am sending this curse out, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. It will go into the house of anyone who steals and the house of anyone who swears falsely by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. It will stay in that house until it destroys it completely, both the wood and the stones."

decisions.choice: I have sent it out: the curse is already on its way
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act: the LORD has released the curse, and it is flying (verse 1). It can also be read as a firm promise of what he will do.

decisions.choice: it will lodge in the house and consume it, timber and stones: like a plague that destroys a house
decisions.reason: The verb "lodge" means to stay overnight. The curse settles in the house and does not leave until nothing is left. The law about a house with a spreading growth in its walls ordered it torn down, "its stones, its timber and all the plaster" (Leviticus 14:45). The wrongdoer's house, built with stolen goods or false oaths, will not stand.

decisions.choice: swears by my name falsely: uses the LORD's name to make a lie seem true
decisions.reason: An oath in the LORD's name called on him as witness. To swear falsely by it was to make God a party to a lie (Leviticus 19:12; Jeremiah 7:9). The thief wrongs a neighbor; the false swearer wrongs both a neighbor and God.

decisions.choice: their / his (L); anyone who (B, R)
decisions.reason: The thief and the false swearer may be any man or woman, so Literal gives "his house" the gender setting, and Balanced and Readable say "anyone who" and "that house". Readable says "this curse" for "it", and "until it destroys it completely" for "consume". The closing quotation mark ends the angel's words begun in verse 3.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֕א הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י שָׂ֣א נָ֤א עֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מָ֖ה הַיּוֹצֵ֥את הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And went out the angel who talks with me and said to me, Lift up now your eyes and see what [is] this going out.
pieces: Then the angel who talked with me stepped forward and told me, "Look up and see what this is that is coming out."

L.5: And the angel who talked with me went out and said to me, "Lift up your eyes, please, and see what this [is] that is going out."

R.5: Then the angel who talked with me came forward. He said, "Look up and see what is coming out."

decisions.choice: the seventh vision: wickedness shut in a basket and carried off to Babylon
decisions.reason: Zechariah sees a measuring basket with a woman inside it. The angel calls her Wickedness, shuts her in, and two winged women carry the basket away to Shinar, where a house is built for it (verses 6-11). The flying scroll purged wrongdoers from the land; this vision removes wickedness itself, and sends it back to the land of the exile.

decisions.choice: going out: the same verb used for the angel, the curse and the basket
decisions.reason: The angel goes out, and the thing he points to is "going out", as the curse was in verse 3. The repeated verb ties the visions together: what is evil leaves the land.

decisions.choice: stepped forward (B); came forward (R); Look up (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "stepped forward" and "came forward", since the angel steps into view, and "Look up" for "lift up your eyes", as in 2:1. "Please" is left to the tone, as in 1:4.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֖ר מַה־הִ֑יא וַיֹּ֗אמֶר זֹ֤את הָֽאֵיפָה֙ הַיּוֹצֵ֔את וַיֹּ֕אמֶר זֹ֥את עֵינָ֖ם בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And I said, What [is] it? And he said, This [is] the ephah going out. And he said, This [is] their eye in all the land.
pieces: I asked, "What is it?" He said, "This is an ephah basket coming out." He added, "This is what they are like throughout the land."

L.6: Then I said, "What [is] it?" He said, "This [is] the ephah going out." And he said, "This [is] their eye in all the land."

R.6: I asked, "What is it?" He said, "It is a large basket for measuring grain, and it is coming out." He also said, "This shows what the people all over the land are like."

decisions.choice: the ephah: a basket or container that held an ephah of grain
decisions.reason: An ephah was a measure for grain and flour, about 20 quarts by the reckoning used in the published books. Here the word means the container that held that amount, large enough for a woman to sit in (verse 7). Since a measure is used in trade, some see in it a hint of the cheating in business the prophets condemned (Amos 8:5; Micah 6:10-11).

decisions.choice: their eye: what they look like, their appearance
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "their eye", which can mean their look or appearance (Leviticus 13:55; Numbers 11:7), that is, what the people of the land are like. The Greek and Syriac translations read "their iniquity", a word that differs by one letter, which is very similar in shape in Hebrew writing. That reading makes the angel's meaning plainer, and many follow it. The translation keeps the Hebrew, whose sense is close: the basket shows the evil found throughout the land. This description of the ancient translations is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: the ephah (L); an ephah basket (B); a large basket for measuring grain (R); their eye (L); what they are like (B, R)
decisions.reason: The ephah is a container here, not an amount, so it takes no units setting. Literal keeps the Hebrew words; Balanced and Readable say what is meant. The basket keeps its image at every level.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֛ה כִּכַּ֥ר עֹפֶ֖רֶת נִשֵּׂ֑את וְזֹאת֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֔ת יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בְּת֥וֹךְ הָאֵיפָֽה׃
records.gloss: And look, a round cover of lead was lifted up, and this [was] a woman, one, sitting in [the] midst of the ephah.
pieces: Then the lead cover was lifted, and there was a woman sitting inside the basket.

L.7: And look, a round lid of lead was lifted up, and there was a woman sitting in the middle of the ephah!

R.7: Then the lead cover of the basket was lifted, and I saw a woman sitting inside it.

decisions.choice: a round lid of lead: a heavy disk of lead used as a cover
decisions.reason: The word means something round: a round loaf, a round district, or a disk of metal used as a weight, the talent (Exodus 25:39). Here it is a lead disk covering the basket. Lead is heavy, and the cover is meant to keep in what is inside.

decisions.choice: a woman: one woman, a figure in the vision
decisions.reason: "One woman" here means simply "a woman". Verse 8 says who she stands for.

decisions.choice: Then (B, R); look (L)
decisions.reason: As in 2:7, Balanced and Readable show "look" with "then" and say what Zechariah saw.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ זֹ֣את הָרִשְׁעָ֔ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֥ךְ אֹתָ֖הּ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ הָֽאֵיפָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֛ךְ אֶת־אֶ֥בֶן הָעֹפֶ֖רֶת אֶל־פִּֽיהָ׃ס
records.gloss: And he said, This [is] the wickedness. And he threw her into [the] midst of the ephah, and threw the stone of the lead on its mouth.
pieces: He said, "This is Wickedness." Then he pushed her back down into the basket and pressed the lead cover down over its opening.

L.8: And he said, "This [is] Wickedness." And he cast her into the midst of the ephah, and cast the lead weight upon its mouth.

R.8: The angel said, "This woman is Wickedness." Then he pushed her back down into the basket and slammed the heavy lead cover over the top.

decisions.choice: Wickedness: all the wrongdoing of the land, pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: The word means wickedness or guilt. In Hebrew it is a feminine noun, so in the vision it takes the form of a woman, as wisdom and folly are pictured as women in Proverbs (Proverbs 9:1-6, 13-18). The figure stands for the sin of the whole land, not for women. The angel names her, shuts her in, and in the verses that follow she is carried away.

decisions.choice: thrown back and shut in: wickedness is held fast so that it cannot escape
decisions.reason: The woman seems to rise when the lid is lifted, and the angel forces her back and seals the basket with the heavy lead. Wickedness is no longer free in the land; it is under God's control and about to be removed.

decisions.choice: Wickedness, capitalized, at every level
decisions.reason: The angel uses the word as a name for the woman in the vision, so it is capitalized. Readable says "This woman is", and "the heavy lead cover" for "the weight of lead", to keep the picture clear.

records.source: וָאֶשָּׂ֨א עֵינַ֜י וָאֵ֗רֶא וְהִנֵּה֩ שְׁתַּ֨יִם נָשִׁ֤ים יֽוֹצְאוֹת֙ וְר֣וּחַ בְּכַנְפֵיהֶ֔ם וְלָהֵ֥נָּה כְנָפַ֖יִם כְּכַנְפֵ֣י הַחֲסִידָ֑ה וַתִּשֶּׂ֨אנָה֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֵיפָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבֵ֥ין הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, two women going out, and wind in their wings, and they had wings like [the] wings of the stork; and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heavens.
pieces: Then I looked up, and there were two women coming out, with the wind in their wings. They had wings like a stork's wings, and they lifted the basket up between earth and sky.

L.9: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, two women coming out, with wind in their wings; and they had wings like the wings of the stork, and they lifted the ephah between the earth and the heavens.

R.9: Then I looked up and saw two women flying out with the wind in their wings. Their wings were like the wings of a stork. They lifted the basket up into the air, between the earth and the sky.

decisions.choice: the stork: a large bird with broad, strong wings
decisions.reason: The stork is a large bird that migrates over the land of Israel in spring and autumn, flying great distances (Jeremiah 8:7). Its wide wings suit the carrying of a heavy load far away. The law counts it among the unclean birds (Leviticus 11:19), which some see as fitting for those who carry wickedness.

decisions.choice: wind in their wings: the wind carries them
decisions.reason: The word means wind, breath or spirit. Here it is the wind that fills their wings and carries them, so that the basket is lifted and borne away.

decisions.choice: two women: bearers in the vision, not explained
decisions.reason: The angel does not say who the women are. They are simply the means by which the basket is carried away. Like the woman in the basket, they are part of the picture.

decisions.choice: I looked up (B, R); between earth and sky (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "looked up", as in 2:1, and "sky" for "heavens", which here means the air above the earth.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֕ר אֶל־הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י אָ֛נָה הֵ֥מָּה מֽוֹלִכ֖וֹת אֶת־הָאֵיפָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I said to the angel who talks with me, Where [are] they taking the ephah?
pieces: I asked the angel who talked with me, "Where are they taking the basket?"

L.10: And I said to the angel who talked with me, "Where are they taking the ephah?"

R.10: I asked the angel who talked with me, "Where are they taking the basket?"

decisions.choice: where are they taking it: the prophet's last question in this vision
decisions.reason: Zechariah asks where wickedness is going, and the angel's answer in verse 11 ends the vision.

decisions.choice: the basket (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for the ephah basket follows verse 6.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י לִבְנֽוֹת־לָ֥הֿ בַ֖יִת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁנְעָ֑ר וְהוּכַ֛ן וְהֻנִּ֥יחָה שָּׁ֖ם עַל־מְכֻנָתָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: And he said to me, To build for it a house in [the] land of Shinar; and it will be prepared, and it will be set there on its base.
pieces: He answered, "To the land of Shinar, to build a house for it. When the house is ready, the basket will be set down there on its base."

L.11: And he said to me, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar; and when it is prepared, it will be set down there on its own base."

R.11: He answered, "To Babylonia. A temple will be built for it there. When the temple is ready, the basket will be set there on its stand."

decisions.choice: the land of Shinar: Babylonia
decisions.reason: Shinar is the old name of the land of Babylon (Genesis 10:10; 11:2, where the tower of Babel was built; Daniel 1:2). It is the place of human pride against God and the place of Judah's exile. Wickedness is sent back to the land it came from, and the land of Judah is left clean.

decisions.choice: a house ... on its base: a shrine where the basket will stand like an idol
decisions.reason: "House" is the word for a temple as well as a home, and the base is a stand or pedestal (the same word is used for the stands of Solomon's temple, 1 Kings 7:27). Wickedness will be set up in Babylon like an idol in its shrine, while in Jerusalem the LORD's house is being built.

decisions.choice: Babylonia (R); a temple (R); stand (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "Babylonia" for Shinar and "temple" for "house", which is what the house is (m2). Balanced and Readable name "the house" and "the basket" where the Hebrew says "it".
